<SUMMARY>
The week of May 29 - June 05, 2026, was dominated by developments in the AI and semiconductor industries, heightened geopolitical tensions in West Asia, and strategic economic moves by the United States and China. AI chip demand surged, with SK Hynix planning to double memory capacity and Google committing $920 million monthly to SpaceX for compute. This demand has spurred warnings of new supply chain bottlenecks, particularly in Taiwan, and fueled strategic competition between the US and China over semiconductor export controls and printed circuit board (PCB) supply. West Asia experienced fresh strikes on Kuwait and Oman, undermining de-escalation hopes with Iran and keeping oil markets volatile, contributing to a sharp decline in US tech stocks. India emerged as a significant investment destination for data centers and technology, attracting $30 billion from AirTrunk and ¥10 trillion from Sumitomo Corporation. President Trump utilized wartime powers to invest $700 million in the US coal industry, while also approving $1.15 trillion in defense spending and advocating for accelerated AI use in the military.
</SUMMARY>
<EWS>
Rising Middle East tensions, marked by fresh strikes on Kuwait and Oman, undermine hopes of a U.S.-Iran de-escalation and contribute to significant volatility in global oil markets. The US strategy of targeting China's printed circuit board (PCB) grip raises immediate supply chain risks for critical AI and defense applications. Taiwan AI firms are warning of new supply chain bottlenecks amid the demand boom, signaling potential disruptions for the broader technology sector. Public skepticism and fear surrounding the AI revolution persist, as highlighted by discussions at the Trump administration’s AI Honors Gala. President Trump's $700 million investment in the US coal industry, utilizing wartime powers, risks taxpayer funds on a sector facing long-term decline.
</EWS>
<EXEC>

**Asia:**
Hong Kong ETFs experienced a record 24.6 billion yuan outflow as investors shifted focus to domestic AI and semiconductor stocks, signaling a strategic pivot in China's economic priorities and investor confidence. SK Hynix received strong backing from investors for its US listing plan and was already planning to double memory production capacity by 2030 and 2031, even before Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's request for more. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang arrived in South Korea, promising "some surprises" and predicting robotics will be the country's next major growth sector. China hit back at US semiconductor export controls, with the Xinhua News agency stating that US abuse of these controls disrupts global semiconductor industrial and supply chains. The US targets China's PCB grip, raising AI and defense supply risks, while a Huawei executive credited bans for accelerating domestic chip independence. Taiwan AI firms warned of new supply chain bottlenecks amid the demand boom, and Broadcom's AI Chip Guidance raised APAC supply-chain questions.

**Europe:**
Europe has learned to live with great-power politics, navigating the complex dynamics of global competition.

**Americas:**
President Trump announced a $700 million coal investment using wartime powers to revive US industry, a move that risks taxpayer funds. Marvell Technology and Flex are set to join the S&P 500 index, replacing Pool and Campbell's, highlighting the growing importance of the technology sector. Google will pay SpaceX $920 million per month for access to approximately 110,000 Nvidia GPUs and related compute infrastructure, an agreement described as short-term "bridge capacity." SpaceX is preparing for its upcoming IPO. Digital infrastructure services startup ITG reported a rise in quarterly and annual revenue in its US IPO filing. Century Aluminum Company announced its participation in the Wells Fargo Industrials and Materials Conference 2026. The Dutch chipmaker Nexperia, facing the loss of its China operations, plans to produce in the U.S. TSMC announced plans for $165 billion in US fabs.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>

**Europe:**
Elon Musk is scheduled to participate in a virtual chat at a private ASML conference next Thursday to pitch SpaceX's Terafab chip moonshot to employees at Europe's biggest tech company. ASML has demonstrated strong market performance, with a $1k investment smashing the S&P at every milestone over ten years.

**Americas:**
Dutch chipmaker Nexperia, facing the loss of its China operations, plans to produce in the U.S.
</LITHO>
<REE>

**Americas:**
America faces an antimony gap, with NevGold Corp. positioning a Nevada brownfield project to help close it through a 20,000-meter drill program underway and a maiden antimony-gold resource targeted for Q2. Brazil sits on one of the largest lithium reserves globally but has barely begun exploration, contrasting with the global rush to mine lithium from Congo and Chile.
</REE>
<GEO>

**Asia:**
Xi Jinping's visit to North Korea is being previewed, indicating ongoing strategic engagements in the region.

**Europe:**
Zelensky offered in-person peace talks in a rare open letter to Putin, which Moscow rejected. Malta held votes, as part of the week's international developments.

**Americas:**
The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) is assessing U.S. military options toward Cuba in the context of a potential next Caribbean crisis.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>

**Americas:**
The House Armed Services Committee approved $1.15 trillion in defense spending. President Donald Trump called for the U.S. military and national security agencies to accelerate their use of artificial intelligence. The U.S. defense semiconductor market is expected to reach USD 11.92 billion by 2035.

**Europe:**
The Europe defense semiconductor market is projected to hit USD 7.18 billion by 2035 amid defense technology investments.

**Oceania:**
US Indo-Pacific deterrence is under strain due to the missile gap problem, as analyzed by The Strategist.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>

**Asia:**
China continues to leverage domestic innovation for chip independence and actively counters US semiconductor export controls. South Korea remains central to the AI memory supply chain, with SK Hynix planning significant capacity expansion.

**Americas:**
The United States is aggressively pursuing AI compute capacity, exemplified by Google's substantial commitment to SpaceX, and President Trump is focusing on domestic industry revival, including a significant investment in coal. Defense spending remains a high priority, with a substantial budget approved and a call for accelerated AI integration in military operations.

**Europe:**
Europe is strategically shaping its semiconductor sector through initiatives like Chips Act 2.0, aiming to center demand, and is home to critical technology companies like ASML.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
Indian shoppers are increasingly favoring compact product packaging due to rising inflation and shrinking budgets, prompting fast-moving consumer goods firms to innovate in response to increased raw material costs. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi may visit India in July for an annual summit aimed at boosting cooperation in security and economic matters, with discussions focusing on China's increasing influence and energy security. Hindustan Zinc plans to double its metal reserves from 13 million tonnes to 50 million tonnes, supporting a mine life of over 25 years and aiming to double capacity and revenue. Blackstone-backed AirTrunk, which did not operate in India six weeks prior, now plans to invest more than INR 3,000 billion ($30 billion) in India by 2030 to build hyperscale data centers, positioning the country as "AI’s next construction site." External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met with Shingo Ueno, CEO of Sumitomo Corporation, who stated the company can invest ¥10 trillion in India over the next decade, exploring collaborative investments to bolster India's goal of reaching a Y=10 trillion economy. HCLTech’s Climate Action Grant in the Americas awarded $1 million to Guatemala-based CISP and Argentina-based Aves Argentinas to advance scalable climate solutions. PepsiCo launched Adrenaline Rush energy drinks in India, adding to its existing Sting brand portfolio in the country.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
US stocks ended sharply lower, with the Nasdaq plunging over 4%, influenced by persistent Middle East tensions and strong jobs data. Mahindra & Mahindra reported its electric vehicle business achieved a 2% operating margin in FY26 while dealing with rising geopolitical uncertainty. The VIX spiked over 6% amid tech stock declines and a strong jobs report, reflecting increased market volatility and investor caution, partly due to Middle East tensions. The S&P 500 slipped over 1%, and the Russell 2000 dropped, both affected by Middle East tensions. Oil markets stopped believing President Trump’s peace narrative as fresh strikes on Kuwait and Oman undermined hopes of a U.S.-Iran de-escalation, keeping oil markets on edge. President Trump stated that Iranian leaders have not yet reached a deal with the U.S. to end the ongoing war because they are "strong" and "proud," further adding that the US has successfully prevented Iran's nuclear program, which is "finished" either with a piece of paper or in a more difficult way. Iran's World Cup Team was approved to play games in the U.S., despite earlier visa problems that moved its training base from Arizona to Tijuana. A Palestinian child was killed by Israeli gunfire in the occupied West Bank, and his parents were wounded. Israel reported a sharp rise in workplace AI use across various sectors. Saudi Arabia aims to deploy 400,000 AI chips by 2030 through "Human targets." Experts predict the war in Iran will impact the global economy for years to come, and President Trump’s Iran War Oil Shield is cracking. 19Network introduced the UAE’s first AI-powered newsroom, redefining news dissemination.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
The global geopolitical and economic landscape is increasingly defined by the intensifying AI chip race, which is driving significant investment and shaping supply chain strategies, particularly amidst US-China tech decoupling. Persistent geopolitical flashpoints in West Asia continue to destabilize oil markets and exert a broad influence on global economic sentiment and stock market performance. Concurrently, US strategic investments, such as President Trump's use of wartime powers for the coal industry and accelerated AI integration in defense, signal a pronounced focus on domestic industrial resilience and national security priorities. India is rapidly emerging as a pivotal hub for data centers and technology investment, attracting substantial foreign capital and signaling its growing role in the global tech ecosystem. The interplay of these dynamics suggests a prolonged period of market volatility, technological competition, and regional instability.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
